The protocol selection problem is framed as a structured decision-making process over a discrete set of communication kernels. Each protocol is characterized by its functional semantics—request/response, statefulness, multiplexing, etc.—which form a categorical basis for mapping to use-case dimensions. The guidance kernel is derived from these characterizations and maps them to qualitative recommendations. However, due to absence of empirical validation, the system operates under a qualitative uncertainty model. The failure mode occurs when use-case dimensions are ill-defined or when the mapping from protocol to use-case is non-bijective. The narrative methodology, while useful for exposition, does not support reproducible inference and thus cannot serve as a foundation for GSE's real-time decision engine.
